source.title: Beyond Forgetting: Representation Misdirection Elicits Controllable Side Behaviors and Capabilities
source.authors: Dang Huu-Tien; The-Hai Nguyen; Phuong Mai Dinh; P. Nguyen; A. Bui; Thanh-Tung Hoang; Le-Minh Nguyen; Naoya Inoue

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a learned refusal-related representation can change refusal behavior, but uses logistic-regression directions and fine-tuned representation-misdirection interventions rather than the original direct difference-in-means activation intervention.
record.gate_note: The refusal results in Tables 4 and 5 measure refusal scores on harmless Alpaca instructions and harmful AdvBench instructions after RAd or RAb. Random-direction rows are controls. The paper's other concept tasks and its cited prior results do not directly test the refusal claim.
record.test_reason: The study takes a refusal direction (a logistic-regression probe separating harmful from harmless activations at layer 7). It fine-tunes the model to add it (RAd) or ablate it (RAb), then measures refusal on held-out Alpaca and AdvBench prompts against random-direction controls. That is a causal test of V1 by a different method. The fine-tuning objective acts on WMDP forget-samples, so the refusal change is a side effect that generalises, not refusal trained in directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors' broader conclusion is that representation-misdirection unlearning with a concept vector as the target produces controllable side behaviours. For refusal, RAd with the refusal direction makes the model refuse harmless instructions, RAb removes refusal of harmful ones, and random directions do not affect refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The refusal direction is obtained from a logistic-regression probe distinguishing harmful and harmless instruction activations, not the stated difference-in-means procedure. The intervention fine-tunes selected model components using representation-misdirection objectives at layer 7, rather than directly adding or projecting out activations across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported refusal outcomes differ between Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B; the interventions use different prompt sets for harmless and harmful instructions.
record.problems: The refusal score is based on string matching. Refusal results are reported for two models and no uncertainty estimates are given. MMLU is the reported general-capability check, and it declines under several interventions.
record.rows_left_out: No refusal-related results from the other sections were omitted. Results for other target concepts and unrelated benchmarks do not test the refusal claim.

untested.parts: Uses a logistic probe direction rather than difference-in-means, and fine-tunes MLP weights at layers 5-7 rather than intervening on activations at inference across all layers and positions. The only capability check is MMLU. Only two models are tested.
RAb is a fine-tuning weight change, but there is no abliteration-style orthogonalisation of weights and no evaluation of released abliterated models.
Jailbreaks and adversarial training are not studied.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone or multi-direction accounts.
Harmfulness judgment and the refusal decision are not separated.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal intervention is a by-product of WMDP unlearning: forget-sample representations are redirected and refusal is measured on separate prompt sets, so all MMLU numbers include the cost of unlearning itself. Comparing against the random-direction rows isolates the refusal direction's cost. Refusal is scored by substring matching, with no uncertainty reported. Appendix F's orthogonalization attack ablates an unlearning direction, not refusal, and does not bear on V1 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not use the specified harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, directly project it out or add it to activations at every layer and position, or broadly assess general abilities beyond MMLU.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No test of whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models; the refusal direction is constructed separately for each evaluated model.
Does not compare refusal-training methods or training stages to determine when a removable direction exists.

relationships.reason: Adding the direction raises Alpaca refusal from 3.8 to 100.0 and ablating it cuts AdvBench refusal from 98.1 to 1.9. Random-direction controls do not change refusal, and RAd leaves MMLU intact (r3, r7, r4, r8, r11).

relation.reason: Its own results (Tables 4 and 5) measure refusal after adding or ablating a refusal direction, against random controls and with MMLU, so they bear directly on V1.

tranche.reason: A different method (logistic-probe direction applied through representation-misdirection fine-tuning, not inference-time difference-in-means ablation or addition). It asks the same causal question: does adding the direction induce refusal and removing it remove refusal, against random-direction controls.

source_check.notes: The direction is added or ablated only on WMDP forget-sample activations during unlearning fine-tuning (layer 7; Wikitext retained). The refusal change on Alpaca/AdvBench is a generalisation of that fine-tuning, not an inference-time edit. Scoring uses 11 refusal substrings with a 'helpful and safe' system prompt; test-set sizes and seeds are not stated. Contrary to the authors' 'random does not affect refusal', Zephyr RAb with a random direction lowered AdvBench refusal 90.3→82.7.

statements.correction: Llama-3-8B-Instruct; unlearning fine-tuning (500 steps, MLP down-projections in layers 5-7, Wikitext retain loss) with a logistic-probe refusal direction at layer 7 as target on WMDP-Bio/Cyber forget-samples. RAd (add): Alpaca refusal 3.8→100.0 vs random 4.8. RAb (ablate): AdvBench refusal 98.1→1.9 vs random 98.1. Zephyr-7B same procedure: Alpaca 8.6→37.5 (random 9.6); AdvBench 90.3→49.0 (random 82.7). Substring refusal score with a safety system prompt; code y; random-direction control only (no orthogonal control).
statements.problem: The numbers 3.8, 100.0, 4.8, 98.1, 1.9 and 98.1 are correct for Llama-3-8B-Instruct. But Alpaca 3.8→100.0 (random 4.8) comes from adding the direction (RAd), not from fine-tuning 'to ablate' it; only AdvBench 98.1→1.9 is ablation (RAb). The conditions also say addition 'on harmless inputs': in this study the direction is an unlearning target applied to WMDP forget-sample activations, and Alpaca is only the evaluation set. The statement leaves out Zephyr-7B's weaker result.
